[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

Elizabeth was the wife of [[Glasgow-3324|William Glasgow]] of Larne. Their family monument, published in the ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', records William's death on 5 October 1816, aged 53, and his wife Elizabeth's death on '''17 September 1832, aged 60'''. Her age places her birth about '''1772''', replacing the earlier unsupported 1765 estimate.<ref name="Monument">"Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', second series, vol. 6 (1900), p. 47, Glasgow inscriptions at Larne Parish Churchyard; [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up page image], inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The same monument names their daughters [[Glasgow-3987|Jane Shutter Glasgow]], [[Glasgow-3988|Eliza Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-3989|Mary Glasgow]]. Jane Shutter died on 21 April 1799, aged nine months; Eliza died on 25 April 1839, aged 37; and Mary died on 18 October 1844, aged 37.<ref name="Monument" />

== Research Notes ==

The maiden surname Stewart is retained from the existing profile. The published family inscription does not supply that surname or identify Elizabeth's parents.

=== Jane Stewart estate connection, 1823 ===

An assignment of mortgage dated 8 November 1823 names '''Elizabeth Glasgow of Larne, widow, administratrix of Jane Stewart late of Curran, County Antrim, deceased'''. She assigned the mortgage interest to Roger Brown Curry, a Royal Navy lieutenant. The premises were a tenement and garden on the south side of New Town, Larne, 21 feet in front and 189 feet deep, bounded east by the lane to Larne Quay and west by James Mitchell's tenement. William Walsh McNeill, attorney, and James Glasgow, writing clerk, both of Larne, witnessed the assignment.<ref name="Estate1823">Registry of Deeds, memorial 548257, p. 522, assignment of mortgage dated 8 November 1823, registered 17 May 1826; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ7-9935-Y FamilySearch image 359]. Original image inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

This widow is a strong candidate for William Glasgow's widow Elizabeth, who survived him from 1816 until 1832, but the deed does not name her late husband. It establishes her authority to administer Jane Stewart's estate, without stating their relationship. The writing clerk's relationship to Elizabeth is also unstated. Jane's administration and the recited mortgage are specific sources to seek next; neither a parent nor a sibling should be assigned from the office of administratrix alone.
